history.dynasty: Ancient; exact date and builder unknown (local tradition links discovery to the Nilagiri kings)
history.summary: The Panchalingeshwar Temple is an ancient hill shrine on a hillock of the Devgiri range (part of the Nilagiri hills), Balasore district, famous for five swayambhu Shiva lingas lying inside a shallow natural pool fed by a perennial stream that washes them continuously - a natural abhishekam. To touch and worship the lingas one must lie flat on the wet rock beside the stream. Local tradition says the lingas were enshrined by Goddess Sita during the Ramayana exile; another tradition names the demon-king Banasura, a devotee of Shiva, as their worshipper; a third account (panchalingeswar.com) says the Nilagiri kings found the lingas in the forest long ago. Reaching the shrine means climbing roughly 263-300 stone steps through forest. The site adjoins the Kuldiha Wildlife Sanctuary (elephant country); a Banadevi temple with a self-oozing pond stands on the hilltop. Not to be confused with the Hoysala-era Panchalingeshwara Temple at Govindanahalli, Karnataka, or the Talakad Panchalinga Darshana festival. CSV town correction: the shrine is NOT in Balasore town - it is in the Nilagiri hills, about 27-32 km from Balasore town, with Nilagiri (the nearest NAC) about 8-10 km away. No verified image could be found after genuine searching (the only confirmed Panchalingeswar images were on unreachable hosts) - media left empty. Opening hours conflict across directories (7 AM-6 PM; 6 AM-8 PM; 7 AM-4:30 PM; 6-12 & 5-8:30 PM) - verify locally.

name: Panchalingeshwar Temple
town: Nilagiri hills (CSV town 'Balasore' is the district HQ city; the shrine is ~27-32 km from Balasore town, nearest town Nilagiri ~8-10 km)
town_description: Nilagiri is a former princely-state town in Balasore district, Odisha, the gateway to the Devgiri range of the Nilagiri hills and the adjacent Kuldiha Wildlife Sanctuary. Besides Panchalingeshwar, the town has an old Jagannath temple and small-town markets.

travel.airport: Biju Patnaik International Airport, Bhubaneswar (~180-200 km - verify); Kolkata airport (~230-250 km) is another option.
travel.railway: Balasore railway station (Balasore Junction) on the Howrah-Chennai coastal line, about 30 km away.
travel.road: Regular buses connect Balasore, Baripada and Chandipur toward Nilagiri; after Nilagiri town a short taxi or auto ride reaches the base of the steps. Free entry; no online booking exists (beware fake paid-booking sites).

visitor_information.best_time: October to February - dry steps, pleasant weather, clear stream (per gokshetra); avoid monsoon if touching the lingas matters.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Roughly 7:00 AM-6:00 PM daily (confirm locally - directories quote conflicting hours: 6 AM-8 PM, 7 AM-4:30 PM, 6 AM-12 PM & 5-8:30 PM).
